chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: After leaving Ellington: Washington, One America, Local 47
summary: He worked with his cousin Elaine Jenkins at One America, consulted at the Kennedy Center, then returned to Los Angeles as recording agent for Local 47.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So, after you left Duke in 1970, what did you do then?

I went to Washington, D. C. where a cousin of mine has a consultant firm, and stayed there for a while. Then I went back to Detroit and stayed a while. I had lived in Detroit for a couple of years. And I didn't care much for that any more. So, I finally came back to Washington, D. C. and worked with my cousin in this firm. The firm is called One America. She is Mrs. Elaine Jenkins, who is quite prominent in the Republican field.

And so I worked with her, helped her set up this company called One America. And it finally got going pretty good, and while I was in this job with this company, I got an appointment to the Kennedy Center as the consultant for -- in relations to the public -- Kennedy Center.

And I stayed in that until there was not much use for the field that I had gotten into. And it sort of just faded out. And the Center, which everyone knows is a terrific achievement -- and it was while I was in Washington and working in this firm and at the Center, I got the call from the union, Local 47 in Los Angeles, to come to a job of recording agent. So, I immediately pulled up, and in a week or so I was back to Los Angeles. So, here I am.
That was when you came back here
I've been here two years last February.
